quickSummary: Carboxylic acids are synthesized by oxidizing 1° alcohols, hydrolyzing nitriles, reacting Grignards with dry ice (CO₂), or oxidizing alkylbenzenes. Acid derivative reactivity towards nucleophilic acyl substitution follows: Acyl Chloride > Acid Anhydride > Ester > Amide. SOCl₂ is preferred for acyl chlorides because byproducts (SO₂, HCl) are gases.
summary: Master carboxylic acid synthetic routes, side-chain oxidation rules, and the acid derivative nucleophilic acyl substitution hierarchy.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7. Carboxylic Acid Synthetic Pathways
conceptBreakdown.title: 7. Carboxylic Acid Synthetic Pathways

summaryBox.title: Synthesis Routes
summaryBox.takeaway: 1. 1° Alcohol oxidation (KMnO₄/H⁺). 2. Nitrile hydrolysis (RCN + H₃O⁺). 3. Grignard + CO₂. 4. Alkylbenzene oxidation (Ph-R ──► Ph-COOH if ≥1 α-H).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
CARBOXYLIC ACID SYNTHESES
                                     │
     ┌──────────────────┬────────────┴────────────┬──────────────────┐
     ▼                  ▼                         ▼                  ▼
PRIMARY ALCOHOL OXID.   NITRILE HYDROLYSIS        GRIGNARD DRY ICE   ALKYLBENZENE OXIDATION
$\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{KMnO}_4/\text{H}^+}$ $R\text{-CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} R\text{-CONH}_2$ $R\text{MgX} + \text{CO}_2 \rightarrow$  $\text{Ph-CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{KMnO}_4/\text{KOH}, \Delta}$
$\mathbf{R\text{-COOH}}$               $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta} \mathbf{R\text{-COOH}}$ $R\text{COOMgX} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \mathbf{R\text{-COOH}}\mathbf{\text{Ph-COOK} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{Ph-COOH}}$
conceptBreakdown.content:
- **1° Alcohol Oxidation**: Converted directly to carboxylic acids with acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$.
- **Nitrile Hydrolysis**: $R\text{-CN} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} R\text{-CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+, \Delta} R\text{-COOH}$.
- **Grignard + Dry Ice**: $R\text{MgX} + \text{CO}_2 \to R\text{-COOMgX} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} R\text{-COOH}$.
- **Alkylbenzene Oxidation**: Toluene, ethylbenzene, or isopropylbenzene oxidize to Benzoic acid ($	ext{Ph-COOH}$) because they possess $\alpha$-hydrogens. $t$-Butylbenzene lacks $\alpha$-H and is unreactive.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 7.1 Acid Derivative Reactivity Hierarchy & Conversions
conceptBreakdown.title: 7.1 Acid Derivative Reactivity Hierarchy & Conversions
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ACID DERIVATIVE REACTIVITY HIERARCHY
                      
   $$\mathbf{\text{Acyl Chloride } (R\text{COCl}) > \text{Acid Anhydride } (R\text{CO-O-COR}) > \text{Ester } (R\text{COOR'}) > \text{Amide } (R\text{CONH}_2)}$$

• Acyl Chloride: RCOOH + SOCl₂ ──► RCOCl + SO₂ ↑ + HCl ↑ (Gaseous byproducts!)
• Anhydride:     2 RCOOH ──[P₂O₅, Δ]──► (RCO)₂O + H₂O
• Ester:         RCOOH + R'OH ──[Conc. H₂SO₄]⇋ RCOOR' + H₂O (Fischer Esterification)
• Amide:         RCOOH + NH₃ ──► RCOONH₄ ──[Δ, -H₂O]──► RCONH₂
conceptBreakdown.content: Reactivity in nucleophilic acyl substitution depends on leaving group ability ($\text{Cl}^- > \text{RCOO}^- > \text{RO}^- > \text{NH}_2^-$) and carbonyl electrophilicity. Thionyl chloride ($\text{SOCl}_2$) is the superior reagent for acyl chlorides because both byproducts ($\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$) escape as gases.

quickRevision: Grignard + Dry Ice (CO₂) yields Carboxylic acids.
Alkylbenzenes with ≥1 α-H oxidize to Benzoic acid (t-butylbenzene fails).
Acid derivative reactivity: Acyl Chloride > Anhydride > Ester > Amide.
SOCl₂ is preferred for acyl chlorides because byproducts are gases (SO₂, HCl).
Fischer esterification is an acid-catalyzed reversible equilibrium.
